text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a cluster of toolcall validations that were quietly degraded to a permissive fallback in eu-west around 22:14 UTC. Console shows success but outputs are missing structured fields. This looks like the quiet fallback we rolled last month.
aj: Ugh. Can you paste the earliest example?
maria: here — request id 9f3b2c, model: rw-large, routed -> degenerate-variant, validator flagged missing `items[].id` so we returned soft-fallback. log snippet: `validator: missing_enum(items[0].id) -> soft_degrade=true`
oliver: That explains user confusion — Console dashboard marks the call as ok and cost is billed, but the route shows fallback. We need a clear flag in UI and telemetry.
isaac: +1 on telemetry. Right now sampling strips the validator tag for low-severity events. We should at least increment a counter routed_toolcall_validation.soft_degrade and surface in per-route chart.
aj: For UX: two asks — (1) Console should show per-request outcome: accepted | rejected | degraded, with tooltip explaining what degraded means; (2) alerting for sudden spikes in degraded percentage > 5% over baseline.
console-team: We discussed similar in last sprint. Implementation question: do we distinguish intentional permissive canary from safety soft-degrade? Both look identical in current logs.
maria: Need an extra field on the invoke event: `validation_mode: strict|permissive|canary` and `validation_outcome: ok|soft_degrade|reject`. That way dashboards and rollouts can filter.
isaac: Agree. Also add `validation_reason` string for human-readable tag, and `validation_code` enum for aggregation. Keep codes small to limit cardinality.
oliver: On routing/quotas side — if fallback is to a cheaper variant we should attribute both cost and user-visible quality. Billing should remain with original route but console should show quality delta. Otherwise product teams won't notice impact.
aj: Do we want automatic rollback for canary-permissive if degraded_rate > X? We already have rollouts but they only look at latency/error.
maria: I'd prefer an automatic canary rollback when soft_degrade_rate crosses threshold and the canary was configured to auto-fail. Manual if not.
isaac: Implementation plan idea: stage 1 (telemetry) emit new tags/metrics; stage 2 (console) add per-request badge and per-route degraded_rate chart; stage 3 (rollouts) hook threshold + auto-rollback. Stage 4 (billing) attribution change — needs finance signoff.
console-team: For the UI, small: add badge + filter toggle, and a table column `validation_outcome`. We'll need a migration script to backfill historic sampling; probably only reingest 7d.
aj: Dev plan: api change (events) + backend metrics + console UI. Ownership: eng-platform prop on event shape; eng-releases for rollouts; console-team for UI.
maria: Heads-up to deploy-bot: planning a canary to emit `validation_mode` tag from validator v2 on next deploy.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: validator-service:v2 -> canary on 3 hosts in eu-west at 23:00 UTC.
isaac: Can we also add a small log line when soft_degrade occurs so SRE can grep? e.g., `SOFT_DEGRADE id=... code=... route=...`
oliver: yes, include it and route_id to tie to dashboard.
aj: One more: sampling rules — make sure sampling preserves all events where `validation_outcome != ok`. Otherwise we'll miss spikes.
maria: I'll open a PR for event schema and a short RFC for rollout behavior + alert thresholds. Assigning follow-ups: @aj alerting thresholds doc, @console-team UI ticket, @isaac metrics pipeline changes.
aj: Thanks — let's sync tomorrow 10:30 for quick implementation plan.
isaac: I'll draft the metric names: `redwood.invoke.validation_outcome.count`, tag=validation_code/route/region. Also `redwood.invoke.soft_degrade.rate` computed in dashboards.
maria: Perfect. Closing loop: need stakeholder signoff from product and finance for billing attribution change before stage 4.
console-team: noted. We'll queue the UI work but hide billing attribution until signoff. :thumbsup:
